1. Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon — adjust upward bias by 2–5% for short-term (1–7 day) forecasts.  
2. After sharp price spikes, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect — reduce forecast by 3–8% in the 2–5 day window following a spike.  
3. Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast — apply a 1–3% upward adjustment to the last 5–10 forecasted values.  
4. Mean reversion is strong in the 10–30 day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 30-day average, reduce by 5–10% for the next 5–10 days.  
5. Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — if true outcome shows a drop in the last 5 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% for the next 3–7 days.
